subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What security boundary should OpenClaw enforce for externally or declaratively registered recurring agentTurn cron jobs that can spend provider quota?
rationale: The safe fix changes compatibility-sensitive cron defaults, plugin/declarative scheduling contracts, provider/model spend policy, and possibly doctor/update UX; automation cannot choose that boundary safely.

options.title: Gate external recurring crons
options.body: Keep operator-authored cron.add compatible, but require externally or declaratively registered recurring agentTurn jobs to carry trusted provenance and stay pending/disabled until the operator enables them with an explicit model or accepted default.

options.title: Warn but keep enabled
options.body: Add dry-run/update warnings and model-cost diagnostics while preserving enabled-by-default behavior for compatibility, accepting continued unattended-spend risk.

options.title: Defer to scheduling RFCs
options.body: Hold this issue behind the scheduling provenance and cost-budget RFCs, leaving current behavior unchanged until the broader design lands.

recommendation.title: Gate external recurring crons
recommendation.body: Keep operator-authored cron.add compatible, but require externally or declaratively registered recurring agentTurn jobs to carry trusted provenance and stay pending/disabled until the operator enables them with an explicit model or accepted default.
